content:
The Mixtures & Alligations chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Mixtures & Alligations tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Mixtures & Alligations

The alligation rule, repeated replacement of liquid, and multi-ingredient mixing to a target price or concentration.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Alligation: (cheaper qty)/(dearer qty) = (dearer − mean)/(mean − cheaper).
  • After n replacements of x from V: pure left = V(1 − x/V)ⁿ.
  • Mixing prices c, d in ratio m:n gives mean = (mc + nd)/(m+n).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Swapping the numerator and denominator in the alligation rule.
  • Using arithmetic (not the (1−x/V)ⁿ formula) for repeated replacement.
  • Mixing quantities measured in different units.

questions.q: A goldsmith melts two gold-copper alloys. Alloy 1 has 85% gold and Alloy 2 has 70% gold. In what ratio must they be mixed to produce an alloy containing 78% gold?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set up alligation with percentages: Alloy 1 = 85%, Alloy 2 = 70%, Mean = 78%.
Step 2: Find cross differences:
Difference 1 (Alloy 2 from Mean) = 78 - 70 = 8.
Difference 2 (Alloy 1 from Mean) = 85 - 78 = 7.
Step 3: Ratio of Alloy 1 to Alloy 2 = 8: 7.

Three varieties of tea costing Rs. 120, Rs. 150, and Rs. 200 per kg are mixed in the ratio 1:2:2 by weight. What is the average cost of the mixture per kg?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Apply weighted average formula: Average Cost = (W1*P1 + W2*P2 + W3*P3) / (W1 + W2 + W3).
Step 2: Substitute values: (1 * 120 + 2 * 150 + 2 * 200) / (1 + 2 + 2).
Step 3: Calculate numerator: 120 + 300 + 400 = 820.
Step 4: Calculate denominator: 1 + 2 + 2 = 5.
Step 5: Average Cost = 820 / 5 = Rs. 164 per kg.

questions.q: A jeweler mixes two types of gold. Type 1 has purity of 0.92 and Type 2 has purity of 0.80. In what ratio must they be mixed to obtain an alloy of purity 0.88?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Set up alligation with purities: Type 1 = 0.92, Type 2 = 0.80, Mean = 0.88.
Step 2: Find cross differences:
Difference 1 (Type 2 from Mean) = 0.88 - 0.80 = 0.08 (parts of Type 1).
Difference 2 (Type 1 from Mean) = 0.92 - 0.88 = 0.04 (parts of Type 2).
Step 3: Ratio of Type 1 to Type 2 = 0.08: 0.04 = 8: 4 = 2: 1
